_meta: Reference ANALYSES — diagnostics and controlled probes that are NOT scored on the frozen ruler (so they never enter runs.jsonl), but are part of the experiment record. Each closes or reframes a question. afterIndex = the experiment index it chronologically followed (for placing it on the dashboard chart's time axis at quality 0). Hand-maintained alongside program.md.

analyses.title: Cloud ceiling confirmation
analyses.question: Is coverage locked by the harness, or by the 3B's capacity?
analyses.result: Capacity. Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.6 through the IDENTICAL harness score coverage 4 (vs the 3B's 3) and quality 0.55 / 0.65.
analyses.detail: Held prompt, schema, gold, judge and decoding constant; changed only the candidate model. Coverage moved 3->4 the moment capacity increased, proving the wall is the base model, not the rubric or prompt.

analyses.title: Coverage-blind re-judge
analyses.question: If we stop scoring coverage, does the 3B reach parity?
analyses.result: No. Dropping coverage from the rubric AND the verdict changes quality ~0; the judge still prefers gold 22-24/30. The losses were never mostly about coverage.
analyses.detail: Re-judged stored candidates with the official judge in a coverage-blind mode. The gap is broad, not coverage-specific — coverage is the symptom the judge can name.

analyses.title: Rubric correlation audit
analyses.question: Is the ~1-point gap five independent deficits, or one latent factor?
analyses.result: One factor. Across 1,552 judged sets a single latent quality factor explains 58% of rubric variance; coverage correlates 0.69 with specificity, 0.61 with naturalness.
analyses.detail: Coverage was never a separable axis to target in isolation — it co-moves with the rest, so any coverage-specific fix was structurally unlikely to land.

analyses.title: GAD discriminator probe
analyses.question: Does a teacher-vs-student discriminator key on coverage or style?
analyses.result: Style. Teacher (gold) vs student (draft) sets separate at AUC 0.76 on style features but only 0.62 on content.
analyses.detail: Pre-registered before the GAD run; predicted (correctly) that adversarial distillation would re-learn Sonnet's phrasing register, not its coverage.

analyses.title: Coverage critic — MiniLM probe (Gate 1)
analyses.question: Can a lightweight critic recognise coverage well enough to select?
analyses.result: No. A MiniLM-embedding critic captures only 18% of the oracle best-of-6 headroom on disjoint tasks (0.999 in-sample AUC, but ~random out-of-task).
analyses.detail: Gate 2 (recall) is fine — oracle best-of-6 reaches coverage 3.31 vs 2.94 random. But recognition doesn't generalise: a shallow critic can't recognise the pivotal unknown on new tasks.

analyses.title: FM critic-adapter — pointwise gate (#1/#9)
analyses.question: Does a full FM critic-adapter recognise coverage where the shallow probe failed?
analyses.result: Modestly, not enough. A real LoRA critic-adapter (SFT on 755 task->coverage examples) captures 26-32% of the oracle headroom (best epoch 3: 32%) vs MiniLM's 18% — a soft fail against the 40% bar.
analyses.detail: Capacity helped recognition, but three ceilings cap the route: oracle is only 3.31 at N=6; the on-device critic has no logprobs (so captures even less); coverage-greedy best-of-N trades off other dimensions.
